evidence.docstring: Find all Django models in the project.

problem: "The model classes, found in each app's models.py" reads as every model in the project. find_models only reads files named models.py, so a models/ package is never read, and it only counts a class whose own base is spelled `Model` or `<x>.Model`. A model that subclasses a project base model (`class Product(TimestampedModel)`), at any depth, is missed. The prose is wrong on those paths, and the method's docstring ("Find all Django models in the project") overclaims the same way.
replacement: The classes in each app's `models.py` whose own base is Django's `Model` (`models.Model`). A model in a `models/` package, or one that subclasses your own base model, isn't listed. Expand a model's handle to see its fields.
route_reason: No extractor reads the plugin's detection rules, and an executed example can't show what is missed. Binding a fact would need a new extractor, which is out of scope for a fix to the prose.

evidence.docstring: Find all Django templates in the project.

problem: "The template files under the project's template directories" suggests the directories the project configures (settings `TEMPLATES` `DIRS`, every app's `templates/`). find_templates ignores settings. It globs only `templates` and `*/templates` directly under each scope root, and it lists only `*.html` files. A template directory that sits deeper (`src/app/templates`) or is configured elsewhere is missed, and so is a template with another extension (`.txt`, `.xml`).
replacement: The `.html` files in a `templates` directory at a scope root or one level below it (`<app>/templates`). Template directories set in Django's settings aren't read.
route_reason: The glob patterns are local to the method, so no extractor reads them, and an executed example can't show the directories it skips.
